subject: Post-call: BrightBridge Dedicated sizing, token economics & next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Anthony Mendoza <anthony@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: BrightBridge Dedicated sizing, token economics & next steps

Anthony / Will — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. I focused this on the cost/throughput tradeoffs we discussed and a pragmatic pilot path.

Call highlights (short):
- Target workload: user-chat + retrieval-augmented answers, average generation ~280 tokens, median context ~1.2k tokens.
- Target latency: P95 end-to-end <300ms for single-turn queries.
- Volume signals: pilot expectation ≈ 20M tokens/month; steady-state planning range 20–60M tokens/month.
- Business target: aimed blended target ~USD 3.50 / 1M tokens for steady-state. You said procurement prefers an anchor number to evaluate viability.

Preliminary capacity recommendations (for discussion):
- Pilot: 1x A100-80GB reserved lane (2-week pilot) to validate latency and token profiles with real traffic and prefix/KV caching enabled.
- Production options (committed):
  • Option A (cost-balanced): 4x A100-80GB reserved — good for predictable throughput and straightforward memory for longer context. Estimated blended unit ~USD 6–7 / 1M tokens at 20M tokens/month (see attached projection).
  • Option B (performance-first): 2x H100 reserved (higher single-GPU throughput) — lower blended unit at higher commit; estimated ~USD 4.5–5.5 / 1M tokens at 20M tokens/month.

Key assumptions driving the numbers (we’ll validate in pilot):
- Continuous batching + prefix cache for repeated retrieval queries (saves ~15–30% on token generation cost for repeated contexts).
- Avg generation length 280 tokens; tail traffic (longer generations) will raise CPU/GPU time.
- We amortized infra and reserved pricing across projected token volume — lower $/1M requires higher committed tokens or more efficient GPU mix.

Next steps I recommend (concrete):
1) Sign pilot SOW (2 weeks, 1x A100 reserved) — Redwood to provide test harness and a small traffic injection plan.
2) Exchange sample prompt logs and one canonical eval set (20–30 prompts) so Ben can pre-run microbenchmarks this week.
3) Follow-up call next Wednesday (UTC-friendly window) to review pilot benchmarks and pick commit option.

I attached a short projection workbook (brightbridge-dedicated-projection-20270525.xlsx) with the back-of-envelope math and sensitivity to token volumes. Ben / Vivek: please add any technical caveats below.

Best,
Laura
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0118

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anthony Mendoza <anthony@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightBridge Dedicated sizing, token economics & next steps

Laura / Anthony — quick technical addendum to the pilot and the two production options:

1) Pilot configuration details (what we’ll ship):
- Model variant: openly agreed model (we’ll pick a 8B–16B family variant for the pilot) to mirror production behavior; will provide exact binary we test on.
- Runtime: single reserved lane, continuous batching enabled, KV cache warmed for repeated retrieval IDs.
- Logging: token-level cost trace + endpoint latency P50/P95/P99.

2) Throughput and efficiency notes (back-of-envelope):
- A100-80GB: good memory headroom for 1.2k context; expect ~10–15% variance depending on request shape. For your mix (280-token generative avg) we model effective output capacity ~30–50M tokens/day across 4x GPUs (highly workload dependent).
- H100: roughly 1.3–1.6x throughput vs A100 on FP16 paths for small-medium batches; better if you can tolerate higher reservation cost.

3) Unit economics framing (sensitivity):
- Baseline math in the spreadsheet assumes steady-state 20M tokens/month. At that volume:
  • 4x A100 reserved -> blended estimate USD ~6.8 / 1M tokens
  • 2x H100 reserved -> blended estimate USD ~5.1 / 1M tokens
- If you scale to ~50M tokens/month the blended unit drops ~20–35% depending on cache hit rate and batch sizing.

4) Risk items to validate in pilot:
- Real prompt shape (we need the logs you mentioned) — longer context increases memory pressure and can push you from an A100 fit into H100/extra-A100.
- Concurrency profile and tail latency under burst (we’ll run a k6-style burst test and report).

I’ll prep the microbench harness once we get the sample logs. Happy to join the pilot kickoff call.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Anthony Mendoza <anthony@brightbridge.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Will Chen <will.chen@brightbridge.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightBridge Dedicated sizing, token economics & next steps

Thanks Laura / Ben — this is helpful and aligns with what we hoped to see. A few follow-ups from our side:

- We can provision an eval dataset and dump ~48 hours of production traffic (anonymized) for your microbench. Will aim to share by end of day Thursday.
- Procurement note: our CFO wants an anchor for short-term budgeting — USD 25k–40k / month is the budget band they’ll consider for the first 3–6 months. Can you confirm which of your options is plausible inside that band?
- Also curious on minimum commit length for a discounted committed plan (we prefer 6 months if that improves the blended unit).

If Option B (2x H100) is substantially outside that 25k–40k band at 20M tokens/mo, we may need to plan a staged approach (pilot -> 2x A100 -> scale) instead of jumping to H100.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the SOW.

— Anthony
Head of AI Platform | BrightBridge Labs
anthony@brightbridge.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anthony Mendoza <anthony@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 17:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightBridge Dedicated sizing, token economics & next steps

Thanks — quick cost sanity check for Anthony:

- At the 25k–40k/month procurement band, the immediately feasible committed lanes are likely a 2x A100 package or a 1x H100 with autoscale burst. The blended $/1M token will be higher at the low end of that band (~USD 8–12 / 1M) but improves as you push to 40k+/month or a 6-month commit.
- If BrightBridge can commit 40k+/month for 6 months, we can model a 2x H100 scenario that pushes blended closer to your 3.5 target.

Proposed micro next-steps:
1) Anthony -> share anonymized 48h logs by Thu EOD.
2) Laura -> I'll draft two short commit scenarios (2x A100 @ 6mo, 2x H100 @ 6mo) with clear blended $/1M for 20/35/60M token buckets and send by Friday.
3) Ben -> start the microbench harness once logs arrive.

I’ll attach the cost model we used to the Drive link.

— Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
